summary.tldr: Requires the Minister of Industry to develop a national framework on the durability and repairability of electronic products and essential home appliances, with reports to Parliament.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Industry to develop the framework after consulting provincial consumer protection representatives and, if appropriate, consumer advocacy groups, for products sold in Canada, whether made here or imported.

Requires the framework to promote durability, explain useful life and repair options, and set national standards for minimum useful life, labelling, maintenance, repair, replacement parts, technical documents, and software support.

Requires the framework to set out consumer responsibilities for manufacturers, importers, and distributors, and to consider legislative measures such as inspection rules and penalties for non-compliance.
Requires the minister to prepare a report setting out the framework within 18 months after the Act comes into force, table it in both Houses, and publish it on the Department of Industry website.
Requires the minister, within five years after the first report is tabled, to review how the framework is working and to table and publish a second report with findings and recommendations.
